title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 180
paragraphs: The Troizenian ship, under the command of Prexinos, was pursued and captured at once by the barbarians. They then took the handsomest of her fighting men and cut his throat at the prow of the ship, treating it as a good omen that the first Greek they had captured was preeminent for beauty. The name of this sacrificed man was Leon — and perhaps his name itself played some part in what befell him.
